New Temporary & Permanent Course Email
The New Temporary & Permanent Course Email is distributed to all faculty, deans, and associate and assistant deans on the last weekday of each month. Recipients then have seven days to submit comments to the CASC Chair, GEC Chair, or Dean of the Graduate School regarding any potential or perceived content overlap involving a new temporary or permanent course.
The email serves two purposes:
Provides notice of upcoming Faculty Senate review. Courses included in the email have already been reviewed and approved by their respective College Curriculum Committees and will next be reviewed by the appropriate Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee: CASC, GEC, or Graduate Council.
Provides an opportunity to identify potential content overlap. College Curriculum Committees may review the courses included in the email to identify any potential or perceived overlap with courses offered or proposed by other colleges. Any concerns can then be raised before the courses proceed to Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee review.

Important Information about Changing a Program’s Academic Calendar
If a program is currently offered on the Traditional Academic Calendar and you would like to move it to the Accelerated Academic Calendar, you cannot simply change the calendar while students are still enrolled in the program. The existing program must first be fully taught out. This requires a proposal to suspend admission to the program. Once there are no students remaining in the program, the program can be moved from one academic calendar to the other.

Alternatively, you may propose a new program by cloning the existing program. This approach does not require Board of Trustees approval and is treated as a program modification. Creating a separate program allows students to be appropriately coded according to the academic calendar in which their program is offered (Traditional or Accelerated).

Content Overlap
Tags: courses,programs,specializations
Short Description: Proposers should review existing curricula and ensure that proposed courses, programs, and specializations do not contain substantial content overlap.
Content Overlap
Proposed courses, programs, and specializations are reviewed for potential content overlap with existing curricula. Proposers should review existing curricula and ensure that proposed courses, programs, and specializations do not contain substantial actual or perceived content overlap.
Early consultation with potentially affected academic units may help identify concerns, clarify distinctions between offerings, and support an efficient review process.
A letter of support, which may be provided as an email from an affected department chair, can be uploaded to the Kuali proposal to document (a) that both departments have considered potential content overlap; (b) communication between the affected department and the department proposing the curriculum; and (c) the affected department’s support for the proposed curriculum.

Syllabus
Tags: courses
Short Description: A roadmap for a course that communicates its scope, learning outcomes, expectations, policies, assessments, and other essential information students need to successfully complete the course.
Syllabus
University Manual 8.50.30 Course Syllabi. All instructors shall make available a syllabus in the first week of class, or first day of class for fully-online accelerated programs (8.51.24), to students enrolled in each of their courses. Syllabi components should clearly communicate classroom policies, essential aspects of the course, and expectations of student participation.
University Manual 8.51.24 For online courses taught in the fully-online accelerated calendar, final projects and/or final exams shall be scheduled by faculty according to the learning outcomes of the class and best pedagogical practices for online learning. The calendar of due dates for assignments and assessments shall be in the syllabus and available to students on the first day of class. No final exam or final project shall be due after the last day of the session.
From the Provost:

In addition to satisfying Faculty Senate approved policies, your syllabus communicates mutual expectations between you and your students and serves as a roadmap to successful course completion, including your course scope, expectations, learning outcomes, deadlines, attendance policies, grading criteria, and other important information. Please provide students with information about assessment/major paper/project due dates, office hours, availability of special tutorial sessions, and expectations on individual vs group work. This clear outlining of expectations helps to ensure that students in your classes understand what they are expected to learn, how they will be assessed, and are fully aware of your academic standards. Providing such information can help avoid misunderstanding, frustration—on both sides—and foster acceptance of responsibility by our students

ABM (Accelerated Bachelor to Master's): A pathway that allows students to double-count eligible courses toward both the bachelor's and master's degrees, reducing the time required to complete the master's degree
Kuali: ABM programs are inherited from the master's degree.
4+1: A pathway that allows students to complete both a bachelor's and master's degree in five years. Unlike an ABM, a 4+1 does not include double-counted courses.
Kuali: 4+1s are inherited from the bachelors degree.

Short Description: In Kuali course forms, the Academic Career identifies both the Level level of a course and the Academic Calendar in which it is offered.
Academic Career

In Kuali course forms, the Academic Career identifies both the level of a course and the calendar in which it is offered.
In Kuali, each course must be associated with one Academic Calendar. The course can exist in both, but only the original academic calendar should be listed in the form.
